claim: Lagged partial adjustment provides an interpretable predictor better than persistence, with limited cross-period superiority.
interpretation: Partial persistence and sector-relative price adjustment are established forecasting motifs. The coefficient is phenomenological, not an identified causal relaxation constant.
falsification: Confirmation constant MAE0.105693 beats reference0.108585; uncertainty is group descriptive, no independent-quarter confidence.

known_relationships: Inertial inflation forecasting, distributed lags and activity-inflation relationships are established.
CPI index differencing is a target definition, not a discovery; component accounting closure excluded.

scope: 1990–2026 US selected national seasonally adjusted series. Revised historical values and seasonal factors can incorporate later information. No causal Phillips-curve, policy intervention, operational financial-return or structural-inflation law claim.

claim: Adding employment pressure, shock asymmetry, robust fitting or acceleration does not establish a new stable inflation mechanism.
equation: See frozen attempts003–006 and nested controls.
interpretation: Employment improved a worst-quarter diagnostic while damaging mean transfer; asymmetry traded mean and worst-group performance.
falsification: No causal intervention, revision-free vintages, or independent economic systems; no structural law or demonstrated financial value.
